title: Co-evolution and the hall of fame
summary: Two teams learn from each other. Choose who each brain plays, and keep old champions around so nothing is forgotten.

steps.title: Choose the opponents
steps.body:
Hiders and seekers evolve side by side. A hider's score depends on the seekers it meets, and a seeker's score on the hiders. Each team is the other's teacher, and both get better together. This is called co-evolution.

The starter adds the breeding rules you may know from the Racing course. In Hide and Seek the generation block runs once for each team.

A generation is played in rounds. In each round every brain plays one scored match. `opponents` sets how many rounds each kind of opponent gets, and `current` rounds are against the other team's brains of this generation.

One match can be luck: a good hider can meet the one seeker that happens to look its way. Add `opponents(current: 2)` so that every brain plays two current rounds.
hints: opponents takes a count for each kind of opponent. Kinds you leave out get no rounds.

steps.title: Remember old champions
steps.body:
Co-evolution can go in circles. Hiders find a trick, seekers learn to beat it, and hiders switch to a new trick. The seekers then forget the old one, and a few generations later it works again.

After every generation, the best brain of each team joins that team's hall of fame. In a `hallOfFame` round each brain plays a champion picked from the other team's hall, so a seeker that forgets how to beat an old trick loses points for it.

Press Check: it trains for 2 generations and counts the matches against past champions. There are none yet. Then change the line to `opponents(current: 2, hallOfFame: 2)`.

check.message: Brains should play some matches against past champions.

hints: Add a second count inside opponents, after current.
Change the line to opponents(current: 2, hallOfFame: 2).

steps.title: How long to remember
steps.body:
`hallOfFame(size: ...)` sets how many past champions each team keeps. Once the hall is full, the oldest champion leaves when a new one joins.

The starter keeps only one, so the hall remembers last generation and nothing older. Press Check: after 2 generations it still holds a single champion.

Keep 20 instead. A big hall remembers older tricks. Each brain still plays the same number of matches, though, so every old champion comes up less often.

check.message: Each team should keep more than one past champion.

hints: The size is the number of past champions each team keeps.

steps.title: A fixed yardstick
steps.body:
Co-evolution makes progress hard to see. If both teams get better, the share of time hiders stay hidden can stay flat. If both get worse, it stays flat too.

A fixed opponent tells the two cases apart. The app has a scripted seeker and a scripted hider: hand-written players with no brain, which never change. In `scripted` rounds, hiders play the scripted seeker and seekers play the scripted hider. The lab shows these matches in the Skill check chart, and its lines only climb when the brains really improve.

Add `scripted: 1` to the opponents. The check trains for one generation and reports how long hiders stayed hidden from the scripted seeker.

check.message: Hiders should play some matches against the scripted seeker.

hints: It is a third count inside opponents.
Change the line to opponents(current: 2, hallOfFame: 2, scripted: 1).
